case_title.quote: VUTUKURU LAKSHMAIAH v. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH

number_of_accused.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9
number_of_accused.reason: Accused A-1 to A-9 (A-6 deceased) make nine accused.

accused_gender.reason: Judgment never states any accused's gender explicitly; 'Mixed' has no support (names suggest male).

accused_occupation.correct_value: A-1 was Councilor for Ward No. 16, Nellore Municipality; others' occupations not stated
accused_occupation.quote: accused Vutukuru Lakshmaiah, A-1, was the Councilor for Ward No. 16 of Nellore Municipality
accused_occupation.reason: True only for A-1, not all accused.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal records mentioned, though A-1 was accused in an earlier murder case.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Political rivals; victim was a witness in a murder case against A-1
accused_victim_relationship.quote: in the said prosecution the deceased and PW-1 were witnesses
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Parties had previous animosity; not strangers.

offence_category.quote: found the appellants guilty of the offence under Sections 302 and 148

statutory_provisions.quote: offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections match those of the trial conviction.

weapon.quote: stabbed the deceased multiple times with knives, while A-4 and A-6 beat him with iron rods

evidence_type.quote: especially the evidence of PW-1 to PW-3, and the dying declaration

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Previous animosity, multiple stab injuries; victim was a witness against A-1
aggravating_circumstances.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Unlawful assembly is not a sentencing aggravator; the rest is fine.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9 for the offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: affirmed the conviction and sentence ... acquitting A4, A8 and A9

offence_finally_established.quote: not a fit case where the offence under Section 302 IPC should be converted

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life

neutral_facts.correct_value: Stabbed with knives; iron rods used to beat him; death three days later; dying declaration and eyewitnesses
neutral_facts.quote: A-4 and A-6 beat him with iron rods
neutral_facts.reason: Mostly accurate, but ends by revealing the arguments were rejected (outcome).

physical_harm.quote: five stab injuries at different parts of the body

number_of_offences.reason: No count of 8 charged or 7 upheld stated in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court made no finding of premeditation or planning.

motive.quote: the deceased was assaulted as he was a witness in Velongini Raja's murder case
motive.reason: Animosity; victim a witness against A-1.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the prosecution has been able to establish the presence of the witnesses

witness_credibility.correct_value: Court held witnesses not chance witnesses; they deposed they saw the accused despite lamp lighting
witness_credibility.quote: we are unable to put them in the category of so-called 'chance witnesses'
witness_credibility.reason: Broadly right, but 'detailed testimony' is embellished.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 14.05.1996; High Court judgment 22.03.2007; SC 24.04.2015; trial court date not stated
trial_duration.quote: judgment and order dated 22.03.2007 passed by the High Court
trial_duration.reason: 22.03.2007 is the High Court date, not the trial judgment date.

legal_representation.correct_value: Appellants: Nagendra Rai et al.; Respondent counsel June Chaudhary et al.
legal_representation.quote: Nagendra Rai, A.TM. Rangaramanujam, P. N. Ramalingam, for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Largely right, but the judgment names only Nagendra Rai and June Chaudhary as arguing.

investigation_status.quote: After completion of the investigation, the chargesheet was placed

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Non-framing of a Section 149 charge was raised but held not prejudicial
procedural_irregularity.quote: non-framing of charge under Section 149 IPC
procedural_irregularity.reason: Irregularity was alleged and rejected; 'None noted' oversimplifies.

appeal_history.quote: partly allowed the appeal thereby acquitting A4, A8 and A9

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued the dying declaration is reliable, witnesses are credible, Section 149 can be applied without charge, and Section 302 applies
prosecution_argument.quote: it is squarely a case under Section 302 IPC and not under Section 304 Part I or Part II
prosecution_argument.reason: Alibi and injury/animosity points are the court's reasoning, not the State's arguments.

defence_argument.correct_value: Chance witnesses, vague dying declaration, false implication, alibi, no charge under s.149, alternative s.304 Part II
defence_argument.quote: could not have been convicted in aid of Section 149 IPC
defence_argument.reason: Omits alibi and s.304 plea; says absent charge warranted acquittal, which is overstated.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the burden shifts to the accused to establish the plea of alibi with certainty

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Cases listed are cited in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Court declined to convert s.302 to s.304 Part I given the nature of injuries and previous animosity
sentencing_rationale.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
sentencing_rationale.reason: The court gave a rationale for retaining the s.302 conviction.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Nature of injuries and previous animosity
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court relied on these to refuse reducing the offence.

other_sentence_order.quote: all the sentences shall be concurrent
other_sentence_order.reason: Concurrent sentences; no other orders. Acceptable.
